_comment: Where a generated component deliberately does not draw what upstream draws,
named by the slot the two disagree on and by the reason.
Every other slot on the same page still gates at zero. This is not a
tolerance: it is the list of decisions this pipeline has made against its
own source, each one written down where the check would otherwise report it
every run and teach nobody anything.
A slot listed here that no longer differs FAILS the run: the decision was
reversed, or upstream moved, and either way the list is wrong. A slot that
differs and is not listed fails as it always did.
Adding one is a decision, not a fix. The question to answer first is
whether the difference is the reader misreading upstream — which is what
this check exists to find, and what it has found every other time.

audio-player.default.why: Two differences, both about a library the page has to load. First, `asChild`: AI Elements writes `<Button asChild><MediaPlayButton>` and `<ButtonGroupText asChild><MediaTimeDisplay>`, and this shadcn build is Base UI, whose equivalent is `render` — so upstream draws two elements where the reader draws one, which is the same decision `plan.default` records. Second, media-chrome is a set of custom elements: the parity application installs the package and the browser upgrades `<media-controller>` into a positioned inline-block that clips its own overflow, while the storybook does not ship the library, so the same tag stays an unknown element with no styling of its own. Which media library an application loads is the application's decision, the way the markdown renderer is.

canvas.default.why: Only one side can draw. `<ReactFlow>` with no nodes and no edges collapses to two pixels, and filling it would be a second design rather than a port. The generated component is the board and the background pattern behind it; the panning, the zooming and the fitting are the engine's, and an application that wants them loads the library — the same arrangement media-chrome gets.

chain-of-thought.default.why: Upstream renders two `<Collapsible>` wrappers — one around the header and one around the content — and threads the open state between them through a React context. The disclosure recipe folds a component into one function precisely because its parts have to agree about one id, so there is one collapsible here and the 16px `space-y-4` between the two of upstream's has nothing to sit between.

controls.default.why: Only one side can draw. React Flow's own component reads a store that a mounted graph fills in — the viewport, the nodes, the node this belongs to — and outside one it renders null, which is what the reference does here. Building a graph around it would be a second design rather than a port, which `parity/README.md` forbids and which the `chart` skip already records for the same reason. What AI Elements adds is a box and a class string, and that box is what the generated component is.

file-tree.default.why: The same `asChild` that `plan.default` records. Upstream writes `<CollapsibleTrigger asChild><button className="flex …">`, and this shadcn build is Base UI, whose equivalent is `render` — so `asChild` is a no-op there and React draws a block trigger with a flex button inside it. The reader takes it at its word and draws one element, which carries the button's own class string. Every other slot on the page gates at zero, and so does every pixel.

mic-selector.default.why: Two of a kind. `<PopoverTrigger asChild><Button>` is the same `asChild` that `plan.default` records — a no-op in a Base UI build, so upstream draws a button inside its trigger and the reader draws one element. And the command palette this component folds is drawn closed here and not drawn at all there: upstream reads the device list from `navigator.mediaDevices`, which reports nothing without a permission prompt, so React renders an empty list and unmounts it.

open-in-chat.default.why: The same `asChild` that `plan.default` records. Upstream writes `<DropdownMenuItem asChild><a href={…}>`, and this shadcn build is Base UI, whose equivalent is `render` — so `asChild` is a no-op there and React draws a menu item with a link inside it. The reader takes it at its word: the item *is* the link, which is what lets `open-in-chat` be a component at all rather than twelve wrappers with nothing in them.

panel.default.why: Only one side can draw. React Flow's own component reads a store that a mounted graph fills in — the viewport, the nodes, the node this belongs to — and outside one it renders null, which is what the reference does here. Building a graph around it would be a second design rather than a port, which `parity/README.md` forbids and which the `chart` skip already records for the same reason. What AI Elements adds is a box and a class string, and that box is what the generated component is.

plan.default.why: AI Elements writes `asChild` and this shadcn build is Base UI, whose equivalent is `render`. So `<Collapsible asChild><Card>` and `<CollapsibleTrigger asChild><Button>` each draw two elements upstream, and the second of those is a <button> inside a <button> — which axe reports as nested-interactive and is right to. The reader takes `asChild` at its word and draws one element, so the card is the collapsible and the trigger is the button.

prompt-input.default.why: The class list is not merged at render. Upstream's `cn()` is tailwind-merge, which sees the `cva` table's `justify-start`, the component's `justify-center` and the caller's `justify-between` together and keeps the last — so React's footer draws its tools and its submit button at either end. The generated component writes all three, and which one a browser applies is then stylesheet order rather than the order they were written in. Two of the three are merged where the reader can see both; the third comes out of a table read at render, so merging it needs a merge at render. Every other slot on the page gates at zero.

queue.default.why: The same scroll area as `suggestion.default`, folded as markup with its recipe left behind: Base UI unmounts a scrollbar with nothing to scroll and measures the viewport with a hook, and neither travels with a copy. A fold that carries a hook-owning recipe is the half of phase 3 that was recorded rather than built — see PLAN.md.

stack-trace.default.why: `StackTraceHeader` is `<Collapsible><CollapsibleTrigger asChild>` around a `<div>`, and `asChild` means the trigger is that div — so what upstream draws of its own is the row an error and its buttons sit on, and that row is what the generated part is. The collapsible around it is behaviour, and the disclosure recipe folds a collapsible into one function because its parts have to agree about one id; so it is the caller's to compose, which the moduledoc says. Two ancestors on the React side, and the copy button counted at the path they give it. Every other slot on the page — the whole frame list included — gates at zero. It is also where the 793 px in `pixel-budget.json` come from: this shadcn build is Base UI, whose `asChild` is a no-op — the same thing `plan.default` records — so the trigger is a real `<button>`, a button sizes itself to its content, and upstream's header is 543px wide inside a 448px box. Its message therefore truncates 97px later than the generated one, and the two buttons beside it sit 97px further right.

suggestion.default.why: The scroll area is folded as markup and its recipe stays behind: Base UI unmounts a scrollbar with nothing to scroll and measures the viewport with a hook, and neither travels with a copy. A fold that carries a hook-owning recipe is the half of phase 3 that was recorded rather than built — see PLAN.md.

toolbar.default.why: Only one side can draw. React Flow's own component reads a store that a mounted graph fills in — the viewport, the nodes, the node this belongs to — and outside one it renders null, which is what the reference does here. Building a graph around it would be a second design rather than a port, which `parity/README.md` forbids and which the `chart` skip already records for the same reason. What AI Elements adds is a box and a class string, and that box is what the generated component is.
